sources.title: Astra beats Opus 5.5 on SlopCodeBench, xhigh considered harmful (X article)
sources.note: Full article text read; modified 2026-11-02. Mirrors the repo report; omits the tables.

sources.title: SlopCodeBench update 10/2026 (repo report)
sources.note: Read in full, used as the baseline to find wording and number differences against the article.

cards.source_title: Astra beats Opus 5.5 on SlopCodeBench, xhigh considered harmful (X article)
cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: Astra/Sol models *do* seem to perform better on xhigh, for this benchmark
cards.claim: The article adds a caveat the repo report lacks: Astra and Sol seem to do better at xhigh on this benchmark, so the medium-beats-xhigh result is model-specific (Opus 5.5 clearly), not universal.
cards.evidence_detail: Single runs; Astra 29 to 32 strict at xhigh; but SOL 6 went 30 to 26 per the chart, so the article's Sol remark is looser than the data.
cards.landing: Per-model effort routing, not a blanket downgrade of verifiers from xhigh to medium.

cards.source_title: Astra beats Opus 5.5 on SlopCodeBench, xhigh considered harmful (X article)
cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: XHigh costs 2.11-4.22x as much as Medium in the three complete pairs
cards.claim: Xhigh cost 2.11x to 4.22x medium across the three complete model pairs, and Opus 5.5 did better at medium than at xhigh.
cards.evidence_detail: Three pairs, one run each; Opus 28 vs 25 strict.
cards.landing: Evidence for testing medium effort on harness verifiers and refuters.

cards.source_title: Astra beats Opus 5.5 on SlopCodeBench, xhigh considered harmful (X article)
cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: I ran each model and effort setting once.
cards.claim: Every model and effort setting was run exactly once (one campaign per setting, seed 42), so run-to-run variance is unmeasured and the effort comparisons are single samples.
cards.evidence_detail: Repeated in the article, and the cost chart notes 'No repeated seeds'.
cards.landing: A reminder to repeat harness-effort trials before acting on a single comparison, including P1.

cards.source_title: Astra beats Opus 5.5 on SlopCodeBench, xhigh considered harmful (X article)
cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: One campaign per setting can't tell me how much is run-to-run variation.
cards.claim: He explicitly says the effort result does not prove that more reasoning hurts coding, only that higher effort was not a reliable way to buy more strict passes.
cards.evidence_detail: Hedge wording in the article, matching the report; the title still says 'considered harmful'.
cards.landing: Treat the effort finding as hypothesis-grade when setting verifier effort.

cards.source_title: Astra beats Opus 5.5 on SlopCodeBench, xhigh considered harmful (X article)
cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: GPT-6.1 Medium has the lowest recorded cost at $178.51
cards.claim: Cheapest campaign (GPT-6.1 SOL Medium, $178.51) matched Astra Medium's strict count, while Fable at about 8.68x the cost got three fewer strict passes, so cost and quality are decoupled.
cards.evidence_detail: Recorded cost, not invoice; Fable $1,550.07 with 26 strict vs 29.
cards.landing: Cost-per-verdict thinking when choosing models for reviewers.

cards.source_title: Astra beats Opus 5.5 on SlopCodeBench, xhigh considered harmful (X article)
cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: the benchmark should measure how much garbage models leave in the codebase.
cards.claim: He reverses his first instinct to exclude scratch and temp files from quality scores after Gabe argued that if humans are not reading the code, leftover junk must be measured, so tests, scratch and generated copies get no free pass.
cards.evidence_detail: Change of position, attributed to a chat with Gabe Orlanski.
cards.landing: Closing checks should count leftover scratch files; a cleanliness gate on agent working directories.

cards.source_title: Astra beats Opus 5.5 on SlopCodeBench, xhigh considered harmful (X article)
cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: If we're not reading the code, we need to measure it.
cards.claim: If humans are not reading agent code, the output has to be measured by tooling, which is the case for backpressure and verifier scripts.
cards.evidence_detail: Principle stated while defending the choice to include scratch code.
cards.landing: Measured gates (lint, scanners) in place of self-reported compliance.

cards.source_title: Astra beats Opus 5.5 on SlopCodeBench, xhigh considered harmful (X article)
cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: Opus XHigh has the lowest slop percentage at 77.75%, versus 94.25% for Opus Medium.
cards.claim: Opus 5.5 xhigh left the lowest slop coverage (77.75%) against 94.25% at medium, yet had fewer strict passes (25 vs 28), so effort trades test passing against code cleanliness.
cards.evidence_detail: 28 matched problems, SLOC-weighted; single run per setting.
cards.landing: Effort routing should depend on what the task needs (pass tests vs maintainability).

cards.source_title: Astra beats Opus 5.5 on SlopCodeBench, xhigh considered harmful (X article)
cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: Opus 5.5. XHigh wrote code that was close to ~5x cleaner.
cards.claim: The article's pull-quote says xhigh code was about 5x cleaner despite fewer strict passes; this '~5x' framing is not backed by the 77.75 vs 94.25 percentage figures (about 3.6x lower unflagged share ratio at most), so the headline is loose.
cards.evidence_detail: Pull-quote in both report and article; 5x is not derived from the stated percentages.
cards.landing: Do not rely on the 5x figure; treat as directional.

cards.source_title: Astra beats Opus 5.5 on SlopCodeBench, xhigh considered harmful (X article)
cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: These new models may produce new maintainability anti-patterns that we haven't built linters for yet
cards.claim: The 200+ linter battery was built from patterns of earlier agent-authored PRs, so new models may produce slop that existing linters miss, which means a fixed verifier set goes stale.
cards.evidence_detail: Speculation, with a promised follow-up from Gabe.
cards.landing: Backpressure rules and verifier checklists need periodic refresh against new model output.

cards.source_title: Astra beats Opus 5.5 on SlopCodeBench, xhigh considered harmful (X article)
cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: We're getting better at maintaing a codebase over time (14.8% to 16.3% during may->september)
cards.claim: Strict pass rate rose only 14.8% to 16.3% from May to September, and he expects 'keeping the lights on for a while to come', meaning slow gains in multi-checkpoint maintenance.
cards.evidence_detail: Different subsets are not comparable; this uses the full benchmark v1.0 vs the May official figure.
cards.landing: Plan for verifiers and human review to stay load-bearing; do not assume models drop the need.

cards.source_title: Astra beats Opus 5.5 on SlopCodeBench, xhigh considered harmful (X article)
cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: the agents get the main behavior right much more often than they keep all tested behavior working
cards.claim: Agents get core behavior right far more often than they keep all tested behavior working as requirements change (core 65.8-74.0% vs strict 12.2-16.3%), so regressions are the main failure mode.
cards.evidence_detail: Ten complete campaigns, 196 checkpoints each.
cards.landing: Regression-style verifiers over earlier work in each phase; cold-resume trial checks old facts survive.

cards.source_title: Astra beats Opus 5.5 on SlopCodeBench, xhigh considered harmful (X article)
cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: 36 problems and 196 checkpoints per setting
cards.claim: Sample size moved from 3 to 6 to 36 problems (196 checkpoints), so earlier subset results (including Fable's 30%) cannot be compared; he distrusts his own earlier small-subset numbers.
cards.evidence_detail: Self-correction on comparability of earlier writeups.
cards.landing: Do not generalise from small trials; state sample size next to every harness claim.

cards.source_title: Astra beats Opus 5.5 on SlopCodeBench, xhigh considered harmful (X article)
cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: the pinned v1.0 catalog, the stock just-solve prompt, seed 42, the any-case runner pass policy
cards.claim: For reproducibility he pins catalog version, prompt, seed, pass policy and Docker with Python 3.12 and uv, a pinned-conditions benchmark protocol.
cards.evidence_detail: Repro recipe.
cards.landing: Pin conditions when the harness runs its own effort or routing trials.

cards.source_title: Astra beats Opus 5.5 on SlopCodeBench, xhigh considered harmful (X article)
cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: Each checkpoint counts equally toward the pass rate
cards.claim: Each checkpoint builds on prior checkpoints' code and counts equally, so problems with more checkpoints weigh more; a failure early can persist.
cards.evidence_detail: Scoring rule.
cards.landing: nowhere obvious

cards.source_title: Astra beats Opus 5.5 on SlopCodeBench, xhigh considered harmful (X article)
cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: Astra XHigh has the most strict passes in this snapshot. But it's lead over SOL 6.1 Medium is only two checkpoints.
cards.claim: Astra xhigh's lead (32) over SOL 6.1 medium (29 strict) is described as only two checkpoints, though the table shows three; the article treats the top ranks as near-ties.
cards.evidence_detail: Table says 32 vs 29; he says two, likely comparing to SOL 6 Medium at 30. Inconsistent wording.
cards.landing: nowhere obvious

cards.source_title: Astra beats Opus 5.5 on SlopCodeBench, xhigh considered harmful (X article)
cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: splitting code into more helper functions can lower average complexity without making the code easier to change
cards.claim: Average complexity is gameable by splitting into helpers and fewer lines is not automatically better, so single metrics mislead and need to be read together.
cards.evidence_detail: Caveat on the callables chart.
cards.landing: Avoid single-number quality gates; pair metrics.

cards.source_title: Astra beats Opus 5.5 on SlopCodeBench, xhigh considered harmful (X article)
cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: Part II
cards.claim: He expects a follow-up (Part II) from Gabe and the SCB team with a qualitative slop-pattern deep dive and new linters, and that findings should reach the main leaderboard soon; a live video breakdown with Vaibhav also exists.
cards.evidence_detail: Forward-looking statement; the tweet text notes leaderboard inclusion soon.
cards.landing: Watch for Part II before acting on the slop-metric findings.

cards.source_title: scb-3-effort.png
cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: Single campaigns at different dates/agent versions: these pairs do not isolate effort
cards.claim: The chart's footnote says the medium and xhigh pairs differ in date and agent version, so effort is confounded with time and agent build, and Opus Max and GPT-6.1 XHigh are excluded.
cards.evidence_detail: Chart footnote; the repo text only says 'single runs'. Costs: Opus $193.47 vs $817.04; Astra $261.05 vs $758.62; SOL $245.69 vs $517.32.
cards.landing: Treat the effort finding as confounded.

cards.source_title: scb-3-effort.png
cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: Medium to XHigh: Opus 28 to 25; Astra 29 to 32; GPT-6 SOL 30 to 26.
cards.claim: Strict deltas going to xhigh: Opus -3, Astra +3, SOL -4, so two of three models lost strict passes at roughly 2x to 4x the cost.
cards.landing: Medium-effort trial for reviewers.

cards.source_title: scb-3-pass-rates.png
cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: Strict scores stay low. Core success is much higher.
cards.claim: Chart gives per-campaign strict/core counts out of 196 (e.g. Astra XHigh 32/136, SOL Medium 30/133, 6.1 SOL Medium 29/129, Opus Medium 28/145, Fable XHigh 26/142, GLM 24/130); the chart shows GPT-5.6 SOL XHigh core 139 while the report table lists 70.92% (consistent).
cards.evidence_detail: Core counts from the chart, including 5.6 SOL XHigh 28/139 and Opus XHigh 25/141.
cards.landing: nowhere obvious

cards.source_title: scb-3-pass-rates.png
cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: GLM labeled XHigh from saved config; directory says Max.
cards.claim: The chart footnote admits GLM's effort label comes from saved config while its directory says Max, so one effort label is uncertain; Opus Max and GPT-6.1 XHigh were incomplete at capture.
cards.evidence_detail: Chart footnote; not in the article or the report text.
cards.landing: Verify which effort setting a run actually used.

cards.source_title: scb-3-cost-strict.png
cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: Dates and agent versions differ.
cards.claim: Cost scatter shows 10 campaigns spanning $178.51 to $1,550.07 inside a 12.24-16.33% strict band, with no repeated seeds; GLM 5.3 XHigh $365.13, GPT-5.6 SOL XHigh $753.30; GPT-6.1 uses SOL pricing and Fable had two checkpoints with zero metering.
cards.evidence_detail: Chart notes: recorded cost is not an invoice; Fable cost may be understated by the unmetered checkpoints.
cards.landing: Cost estimates are approximate; do not over-fit routing on them.

cards.source_title: scb-3-final-failures.png
cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: Final strict success does not imply every earlier checkpoint passed.
cards.claim: Final failed test cases per campaign range from 1,435 (Astra XHigh) to 2,831 (SOL Medium), with final strict problems 0 to 3 of 36, so almost no run ends in a fully passing codebase; Skips: 5.6 XHigh 15, SOL6 XHigh 1, others 17.
cards.evidence_detail: Failure categories: most final failures are Regression (e.g. 1,178 of 1,435; 2,479 of 2,831). Only last checkpoint per problem; not distinct bugs.
cards.landing: Failures are mostly regressions of earlier behaviour; verifier should replay earlier tests.

cards.source_title: scb-3-final-failures.png
cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: Each problem contributes only its last expected checkpoint
cards.claim: Opus 5.5 Medium, the core leader (145/196), ended with 0 of 36 strict final problems and 2,508 failed tests, so high core pass does not mean a working end state; Opus XHigh had 2,446 failed and 1 strict final.
cards.evidence_detail: Chart numbers; GPT-6.1 SOL Medium 3/36 strict final with 2,757 failed.
cards.landing: Judge the final state, not stage success.

cards.source_title: scb-3-quality-slop-coverage.png
cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: Ranked by SLOC-weighted heuristic coverage; not a defective-code percentage.
cards.claim: Slop coverage per campaign (main=filtered except Opus Medium): Opus XHigh 77.75, Fable XHigh 82.11, GPT-5.6 SOL XHigh 89.05, Astra XHigh 89.71, GLM 89.86, Astra Medium 90.76, SOL6 XHigh 91.11, 6.1 SOL Medium 91.51, SOL6 Medium 92.58, Opus Medium 94.25/92.90; no model is below 77%, and eight problems omitted for incomplete scanner coverage.
cards.evidence_detail: Chart; 28 matched problems; coverage is a union of AST-rule spans and within-file clone spans over total SLOC.
cards.landing: Quality scanners flag most lines for all models; a metric with little spread cannot gate.

cards.source_title: scb-3-quality-volume.png
cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: Filtered is not a tests-free scope.
cards.claim: Final source volume varies about 9x across campaigns: Opus Medium 216,881 SLOC (175,616 filtered + 41,265 in tests/_work), Fable XHigh 122,504, Opus XHigh 96,632, GLM 91,907, Astra XHigh 76,448, GPT-5.6 SOL XHigh 66,186, 6.1 SOL Medium 44,019, SOL6 XHigh 41,147, Astra Medium 39,988, SOL6 Medium 24,991.
cards.evidence_detail: Native Radon SLOC; no verified test/non-test split; only the Opus Medium snapshot (45 files in dynamic_buffer) changed under filtering.
cards.landing: Output volume is a cheap bloat signal worth capping or monitoring.

cards.source_title: scb-3-quality-callables.png
cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: Callable count is not body length; complexity does not establish correctness.
cards.claim: Callables and mean cyclomatic complexity differ widely: Fable 8,967 / 3.57, Astra XHigh 5,099 / 4.72, Opus XHigh 6,075 / 4.86, GLM 4,883 / 5.78, Astra Medium 2,438 / 6.38, 6.1 SOL Medium 2,531 / 6.38, Opus Medium 13,462 / 7.12, 5.6 SOL XHigh 2,331 / 7.47, SOL6 XHigh 1,803 / 8.74, SOL6 Medium 1,083 / 11.70.
cards.evidence_detail: 28 matched problems; the chart calls the two measures separate, not a combined quality score.
cards.landing: nowhere obvious

cards.source_title: scb-3-quality-callables.png
cards.author: Dex
cards.quote: Missing scans never count as clean.
cards.claim: Scanner policy: missing scans are never counted as clean and both scopes exclude dependency, venv and cache paths, a conservative rule for unmeasured output.
cards.evidence_detail: Chart footnote across all three quality charts.
cards.landing: Unknown-as-fail policy for verifiers, mirroring the 'unknown is not new' completion rule.

gaps: The article does not repeat the report's results tables, so per-campaign numbers come only from the report and charts.
No run-to-run variance exists anywhere in the bundle: one run per setting, no repeated seeds.
The cost chart notes Fable had two checkpoints with zero metering, so its cost is likely understated.
Part II (Gabe's qualitative analysis) and the livestream with Vaibhav were not part of this bundle.
